title: Voodoo Vince
subtitle: The hero's misfortune becomes his strongest attack
summary: Voodoo Vince is Beep Industries' Xbox platform game, released in North America on 23 September 2003. body: Voodoo Vince is Beep Industries' Xbox platform game, released in North America on 23 September 2003. Its hero is a voodoo doll whose ability to hurt nearby enemies depends on the trouble inflicted on himself. Familiar jumping, punching and spinning establish the basic movement, while special powers turn comic accidents into attacks. The setting and Steve Kirk's music give the journey a distinctive character. The central joke also supplies a practical rule: the dangerous object in the room may be something Vince needs to use rather than simply avoid.

Enemies leave beads that fill Vince's power meter, allowing a special attack once it is ready. These powers injure the doll in different theatrical ways while destroying nearby opponents. Environmental puzzles take the idea further by asking the player to activate something capable of harming Vince at the right place. Collectibles improve health, lives and the number of powers available. The player moves between ordinary platforming and situations where understanding the joke reveals the solution, recognising how the surroundings can turn the hero's apparent vulnerability into an advantage.

Clayton Kauzlaric directed the game, whose levels also include vehicles and short departures from standard platforming. Steve Kirk's score helps connect the varied locations through a consistent musical voice. A remastered edition reached Xbox One and Windows in 2017, making the adventure available again after its original Xbox release. The design remains memorable because its unusual premise reaches beyond the character's appearance. Vince's stitched body explains the attacks, the puzzles and the comedy, allowing the game to build an entire journey around a single recognisable physical idea.
